summary: Hashes, re-fetches, verbatim lines, instants and zone all verify clean: 72/72 INDEX.md sha256 re-hashed byte-exact, 9 cited documents independently re-fetched byte-identical, all 313 family rows / 621 product-date comparisons match the saved bytes exactly, every asserted instant literally appears in its own cited document (no instant inferred from another year), and the baselines match the reference-week bytes. Two load-bearing defects: (1) the 'missing' list falsely asserts no post-2024-12-20 archive capture exists for the 2025 holidays - the archive holds 44 captures of the Thanksgiving-2025 window from the 2026-01-29 crawl, and that later operator statement differs from the one recorded on 8 product-dates; (2) the 2025-07-03 Equity Index early close at 12:15 CT is classified 'modified' with no close_instant while the identical pattern elsewhere is 'early_close'.

discrepancies.where: missing[] entry 4 and the RESIDUAL RISK paragraph of coverage; holidays[2025-11-27].families rows for date 2025-11-28 (document D09)
discrepancies.claim_quoted: A post-finalisation operator statement for the 2025 holidays from Presidents' Day 2025 through Thanksgiving 2025. Only the 2024-12-20 capture exists. Channels tried: CDX over the service endpoint (no 2025-window capture later than 2024-12-20 for any of those holidays)
discrepancies.finding: False for Thanksgiving 2025. A fresh CDX enumeration returns 45 captures of the identical service window fromEventDate=2025-11-26&toEventDate=2025-11-28, of which 44 are from the 2026-01-29 crawl (timestamps 20260129012143 .. 20260129012309) - i.e. taken two months AFTER the holiday, so a post-finalisation operator statement. It was retrieved (raw/cme-2025-2027.verify/probe/thbp_2025-11-26_2025-11-28_20260129012309.json) and differs from D09 on 8 product-dates, all on 2025-11-28: ES, ZN, 6E, CL, GC and BTC each gain '07:00 preopen; 07:30 open' ahead of the early close; ZC gains '07:00 preopen' before its 08:30 open; LBR gains '07:00 preopen' alongside its 06:00 preopen. The early-close instants themselves (12:15 CT for ES/ZN, 13:45 CT for 6E/CL/GC/BTC, 12:05 CT for ZC/LE/LBR) are unchanged in both publications.
discrepancies.impact: No recorded instant is wrong, but the Thanksgiving-2025 rows quote a superseded publication as their verbatim, the stated residual risk is factually incorrect, and the vintage choice is inconsistent within the task itself (D10, Christmas 2025, was taken from that same 2026-01-29 crawl).
discrepancies.fix: Re-source D09 from capture 20260129012309, re-quote the 2025-11-28 verbatim lines, and narrow the residual-risk paragraph and missing[] entry 4 to the seven holidays where the 2024-12-20 capture really is the only one (New Year 2025, MLK, Presidents', Good Friday, Memorial, Juneteenth, Independence, Labor - each has exactly 1 capture, confirmed).

discrepancies.recorded: status=modified, close_instant absent, note [N9], verbatim 'eventDate 2025-07-03: 12:15 closed /TD 2025-07-03; 16:45 preopen /TD 2025-07-04; 17:00 open /TD 2025-07-04'
discrepancies.finding: The cited bytes show ES closing at 12:15 CT on Thursday 2025-07-03 against a normal Thursday final close of 16:00 CT (ZN, 6E, CL, GC and BTC all close 16:00 that day). That is an early final close at a stated instant. The identical pattern on 2025-11-28 ('12:15 closed') is classified early_close with close_instant '12:15 CT'. The task's own working file FINAL_REVIEW.txt line 102 flags the deviation ('ES 12:15 closed |norm: 16:00 closed|'), so the classification was lost between the working file and the published rows.
discrepancies.impact: This is the only Independence-Day-eve equity-index early close in the 2025 set; a consumer keyed on status/close_instant (which is how a holiday table is built under LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE: date, kind, instant) would drop it. Sole occurrence of this class across all 313 rows.
discrepancies.fix: status=early_close, close_instant='12:15 CT', note 'EC 12:15 CT (evening leg runs normally: 16:45 preopen, 17:00 open)'.

discrepancies.where: the 17 rows carrying note [N3] (all status=normal) and 2027-12-23 Cryptocurrency (status=normal, [N8])
discrepancies.finding: N3 is defined as 'ordinary daily 16:00-17:00 CT pause, no early close; no final close on the date so the trade date rolls'. Those dates therefore differ from CME's normal grid twice over: no 16:00 final close event, and the pre-open starts 16:00 rather than 16:45, so the holiday has no trade date of its own (e.g. FX on 2025-01-20 carries trade date 2025-01-21 throughout). They are labelled 'normal'. The converse single deviation - final close present, no evening re-open ([N6]) - is labelled 'modified'. Likewise 2027-12-23 BTC is 'normal'/[N8] ('event list equals the normal grid') although its 16:01/16:02 re-open carries trade date 2027-12-27, not the next calendar day.
discrepancies.impact: The underlying facts survive in the verbatim and in the note definitions, so nothing is unsourced; but a consumer reading status alone would record no holiday entry for FX and pre-24/7 crypto on Monday and Thursday holidays and lose the trade-date roll.
discrepancies.fix: Either widen the status vocabulary (e.g. 'no_trade_date' / 'rolls') or label N3 rows 'modified' like the N6 rows.

discrepancies.where: coverage ('Note codes N1..N17 and EC are expanded in raw/cme-2025-2027/INDEX.md') and the 3 rows using [N17] (2025-01-01, 2025-12-25, 2026-01-01)
discrepancies.finding: INDEX.md defines N1..N16 and EC only. N17 ('16:00 preopen; 17:00 open with the next business day's trade date and no day session') is used but never defined.

discrepancies.where: raw/cme-2025-2027/INDEX.md url column for the 27 archive artifacts
discrepancies.finding: The archived URLs carry an '&isProtected&_t=<epoch>' suffix that INDEX.md omits; following an INDEX url literally returns a Wayback 404 (verified). The exact URLs exist only in arc/fetchlist.tsv, which is itself not listed in INDEX.md, together with roughly 110 other files on disk (every .raw reader original, html/*.gz, api/, cdx/ and js/ working files, DEVIATIONS*.json, NORMAL_PATTERNS.json, DEV_REVIEW.txt).
discrepancies.impact: Bytes are all present and the hashes are honest; only the one-step re-fetch path is broken.

discrepancies.finding: CME's own 2025 Globex holiday table states the Thanksgiving period as '27 - 29 November 2025', including Saturday 29 November, but the window retrieved stops at 2025-11-28 and no gap is recorded. The task itself flags special Saturday sessions after Friday holidays (2026-06-20, 2026-07-04, 2027-06-19), so the unchecked Saturday matters. Mitigation: this verification queried the live service for 2026-11-27..29 and 2027-11-26..28 and found no Saturday session after Thanksgiving in either year for any non-crypto group, so the residual risk is low; the 2025 Saturday is not in the archive and can no longer be checked.

The quoted CME statement 'Due to the US Employment Situation Release on April 3, 2026, CME Group Equities, FX, Cryptocurrency and Interest Rate products will have unique Closes and Settlements for trade date April 3rd' is given no document id; the rows for that holiday cite only D14 (the T2 service). The quotation is verbatim at line 2498 of the indexed html/trading-hours-20250830.html, which is a T1 operator page - worth citing, since it is the only T1 corroboration of the 08:15/10:15 CT closes.
